answer: Each agent registers a proof‑of‑stake token that references a unique hardware enclave, recorded on a public ledger we call the lagoon. The system assigns quadratic weight: an ivory‑rated node, verified by a chain of attestations, contributes one full vote, while a cluster of newly minted sparrow identities each adds only the square‑root of its count, so ten fake IDs equal less than one trusted node. An attacker must acquire costly enclave hardware and stake proportional to the quadratic cost, making large‑scale Sybil attacks economically prohibitive.
